newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies finish mixed in lackluster trade. [CORRECTED 21:58 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies finish mixed in lackluster trade. [CORRECTED 21:58 GMT]

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mixed in lackluster trade, with yen contracts rising ahead of Japan's current account trade data on Wednesday, traders and analysts said.
They said growing expectations Japan would post a large current account trade surplus against the U.S. were attracting flight-to-quality buying in Asia.
"The yen is the place to be in Asia," one currency futures trader said. "The yen has become the safe-haven currency in Asia."

U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky expressed concern on Tuesday morning about "disturbing trends" in Japan's trade balance and repeated that the United States does not want a big rise in Japan's surplus.
However, traders said there were strong market ideas that Japan would support the dollar/yen at 111.80 spot, which roughly corresponds to $0.009064 (Corrects from $0.009214) in September yen.
September yen rose to $0.009090, above $0.009060, the 5-3/4-month high set on GLOBEX. Further resistance is at $0.009136, or 111.00 spot yen.
Meanwhile, September marks and Swiss francs remained lower.
September marks widened opening losses after Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima said earlier in the day that the government needed to make some adjustments in order to reach its 1997 budget target.

At the close of pit trade, September yen were up $0.000058 to $0.009029, marks fell $0.0038 to $0.5860, Swiss francs fell $0.0016 to $0.7017, sterling added $0.0030 to $1.6350, Canadian dollar firmed $0.0003 to $0.7258, Aussie dollar edged up $0.0002 to $0.7627, and Mexican peso rose $0.000250 to $0.120100.
